Many optimization problems live on a **network**: nodes joined by arcs, with lengths,
costs or capacities on the arcs. Routing, logistics, scheduling and assignment problems
all have this shape. Network problems are special for two reasons:

- they can be solved by fast **combinatorial algorithms** (labels, paths, augmentations)
  instead of general-purpose LP methods;
- they are LPs whose optimal solutions are **automatically integer**. So these are
  integer problems that are as easy as linear ones.

All pages here use the same small network with six nodes $s, a, b, c, d, t$ (and a
small worker–job graph for matching), so the numbers carry over between pages.

Prerequisite: [LP Duality](../linear-programming/duality/lp-duality.qmd). Integrality
links forward to [Integer Programming](../integer-programming/index.qmd).
